media.title: Sonatina for piano, I — audio reference
media.description: The first movement (Allegro) of Kaper’s Sonatina for piano, dated 1927, the year Róża Etkin performed it in Berlin. The three-movement manuscript, headed Warsaw although Kaper was by then living in Berlin, survives in the Bronislaw Kaper Papers (box 2). The audio is a score-to-MIDI rendering of a transcription made from the manuscript.
media.altText: Audio rendering by Iwona Lindstedt of the first movement of Kaper’s Sonatina for piano.

otherWorks.publisherOrHoldingAsPrinted: Bronisław Kaper, Sonatina for Piano, autograph manuscript, Warsaw, 1927. Bronislaw Kaper Papers, Collection 03193, box 2, American Heritage Center, University of Wyoming, Laramie.
otherWorks.publicNote: The manuscript is headed Warsaw, 1927, although Kaper had moved to Berlin by the autumn of 1926 and Róża Etkin gave the first performance of a work by him at the Bach-Saal in Berlin on 3 December 1927. Kaper headed his manuscripts by place and revised such headings: on the score of Piece for Voice and Orchestra “Warsaw” is struck through and replaced by “Berlin”. The heading is recorded here as it stands, without deciding where the Sonatina was written.
